hints: Apply the generalised binomial expansion to $(1-4x)^{1/4}$.
Simplify each coefficient separately, retaining every term through $x^3$ and checking the signs created by $u=-4x$.
walkthrough:
Rewrite the fourth root with a fractional index:
$$\sqrt[4]{1 - 4x} = (1 - 4x)^{\frac{1}{4}}$$

Recall the binomial series expansion formula for $(1 + u)^n$ with $n = \dfrac{1}{4}$ and $u = -4x$:
$$(1 + u)^n = 1 + nu + \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}u^2 + \dfrac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{3!}u^3 + \dots$$

Compute the constant term and the linear term in $x$:
$$\text{Term 0: } 1$$
$$\text{Term 1: } nu = \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)(-4x) = -x$$

Combine the terms to obtain the expansion up to $x^3$:
$$\sqrt[4]{1 - 4x} = 1 - x - \dfrac{3}{2}x^2 - \dfrac{7}{2}x^3$$
